hook.en: A shopkeeper in Dharwad opens at 8 a.m. every day, while a grandmother tells stories to her grandchildren for free. Both are busy, but only one is doing business. What is the difference?
hook.kn: ಧಾರವಾಡದ ಅಂಗಡಿಯವನು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ 8ಕ್ಕೆ ಅಂಗಡಿ ತೆರೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಅಜ್ಜಿ ಮೊಮ್ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ಉಚಿತವಾಗಿ ಕಥೆ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾಳೆ. ಇಬ್ಬರೂ ಕೆಲಸದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರು ಮಾತ್ರ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವೇನು?

objectives.en: Tell economic activities from non-economic activities
Recall how trade and indigenous banking developed in ancient India

narration.en: A shopkeeper in Dharwad opens at 8 a.m. every day, while a grandmother tells stories to her grandchildren for free. Both are busy, but only one is doing business. What is the difference?
narration.kn: ಧಾರವಾಡದ ಅಂಗಡಿಯವನು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ 8ಕ್ಕೆ ಅಂಗಡಿ ತೆರೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಅಜ್ಜಿ ಮೊಮ್ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ಉಚಿತವಾಗಿ ಕಥೆ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾಳೆ. ಇಬ್ಬರೂ ಕೆಲಸದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಆದರೆ ಒಬ್ಬರು ಮಾತ್ರ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವೇನು?

body.en: Economic activities are done to earn a living or wealth: business, profession and employment. Non-economic activities are done out of love, sympathy, religion or patriotism, such as a housewife cooking for her family or a student volunteering in a flood camp. Business is the economic activity of producing or buying and selling goods and services regularly to earn profit.

points.en: Non-economic: from love, duty, religion or patriotism
Business = regular production/purchase and sale of goods and services for profit

narration.en: Economic activities are done to earn a living or wealth: business, profession and employment. Non-economic activities are done out of love, sympathy, religion or patriotism, such as a housewife cooking for her family or a student volunteering in a flood camp. Business is the economic activity of producing or buying and selling goods and services regularly to earn profit.
narration.kn: ಜೀವನೋಪಾಯ ಅಥವಾ ಸಂಪತ್ತು ಗಳಿಸಲು ಮಾಡುವ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು. ಪ್ರೀತಿ, ಕರುಣೆ, ಧರ್ಮ ಅಥವಾ ದೇಶಪ್ರೇಮದಿಂದ ಮಾಡುವವು ಆರ್ಥಿಕೇತರ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು.

narration.en: All human activities fall into two groups: economic and non-economic.

say.en: All human activities fall into two groups: economic and non-economic.
Economic activities earn money: business, profession and employment.
Non-economic activities come from love, religion or patriotism; no money is the aim.
The same work can be either: a mother cooking at home is non-economic, a hotel cook is economic.
Business has seven features. Remember especially: regular dealings, profit motive and risk.

narration.en: Sort each activity: economic or non-economic.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಅಥವಾ ಆರ್ಥಿಕೇತರ ಎಂದು ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

explanation.en: Economic activities are done to earn a living or wealth; non-economic ones are done out of love, sympathy, religion or patriotism. The same skill can be either, depending on the purpose.

text.en: A farmer sells tomatoes at the APMC market
A doctor treats patients in her clinic for a fee
A clerk works in a bank for a salary
A tailor stitches shirts for customers
A mother cooks dinner for her family
A student volunteers in a flood relief camp
A grandfather prays at the temple
A teacher gives free tuition to a neighbour's child
A tailor stitches a dress for his own daughter

body.en: Every business is an economic activity that produces or procures goods and services and sells or exchanges them. The dealings must be on a regular basis, the aim is profit, the return is uncertain, and there is always an element of risk.

points.en: Production or procurement of goods and services

narration.en: Every business is an economic activity that produces or procures goods and services and sells or exchanges them. The dealings must be on a regular basis, the aim is profit, the return is uncertain, and there is always an element of risk.
narration.kn: ವ್ಯವಹಾರವು ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆ; ಸರಕು ಸೇವೆಗಳ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ಮಾರಾಟ ಅಥವಾ ವಿನಿಮಯ, ನಿಯಮಿತ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ, ಲಾಭದ ಗುರಿ, ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಆದಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಾಯ ಇದರ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು.

title.en: Trade and commerce in ancient India

body.en: India had a rich trading tradition by land and sea. Indigenous bankers used instruments such as the hundi, which worked like a bill of exchange, and the chitti for credit. Merchant guilds and trading communities financed and organised trade across major trade centres and ports.

points.en: Hundi: an indigenous instrument of exchange
Merchant guilds organised and financed trade
Busy ports linked India to distant markets

narration.en: India had a rich trading tradition by land and sea. Indigenous bankers used instruments such as the hundi, which worked like a bill of exchange, and the chitti for credit. Merchant guilds and trading communities financed and organised trade across major trade centres and ports.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರಾಚೀನ ಭಾರತದಲ್ಲಿ ಭೂ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮುದ್ರ ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ಸಮೃದ್ಧವಾಗಿತ್ತು. ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕರುಗಳು ಹುಂಡಿಯಂತಹ ವಿನಿಮಯ ಸಾಧನಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು.

caption.en: Households supply labour and buy goods; firms produce goods and pay incomes. Business keeps this flow of goods and money moving.
caption.kn: ಕುಟುಂಬಗಳು ಶ್ರಮವನ್ನು ಪೂರೈಸಿ ಸರಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಖರೀದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳು ಸರಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸಿ ಆದಾಯ ಪಾವತಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಈ ಸರಕು ಮತ್ತು ಹಣದ ಹರಿವನ್ನು ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿಡುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Classify: (a) Ravi buys umbrellas from a Mangaluru wholesaler every monsoon and sells them at his stall. (b) Meena knits sweaters for her own children. (c) Sunil sells his old cycle once to a neighbour.

steps.en: (a) Regular purchase and sale with a profit motive: business activity.
(b) Done out of love for her children, not to earn: non-economic activity.
(c) An isolated, one-time sale lacks regular dealings: not business.

narration.kn: ತರಗತಿ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಪಕ್ಕದವರೊಂದಿಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಕೈ ಎತ್ತಿ, ಮಾನಿಟರ್ ತರಗತಿಯ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಲಿ.

points.en: Economic activities earn a living; non-economic ones come from love, duty or faith.
points.kn: ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು ಜೀವನೋಪಾಯಕ್ಕಾಗಿ; ಆರ್ಥಿಕೇತರ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು ಪ್ರೀತಿ, ಕರ್ತವ್ಯ ಅಥವಾ ನಂಬಿಕೆಯಿಂದ.

points.en: Business needs regular dealings, a profit motive, and it always carries risk.
points.kn: ವ್ಯವಹಾರಕ್ಕೆ ನಿಯಮಿತ ವಹಿವಾಟು, ಲಾಭದ ಉದ್ದೇಶ ಬೇಕು; ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಅಪಾಯವಿದೆ.

points.en: The return in business is uncertain.
Ancient Indian trade used instruments like the hundi.
points.kn: ಪ್ರಾಚೀನ ಭಾರತೀಯ ವ್ಯಾಪಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಹುಂಡಿಯಂತಹ ಸಾಧನಗಳು ಬಳಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದವು.

narration.en: Recap. Economic activities earn a living; non-economic ones come from love, duty or faith. Business needs regular dealings, a profit motive, and it always carries risk. The return in business is uncertain. Ancient Indian trade used instruments like the hundi.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು ಜೀವನೋಪಾಯಕ್ಕಾಗಿ; ಆರ್ಥಿಕೇತರ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳು ಪ್ರೀತಿ, ಕರ್ತವ್ಯ ಅಥವಾ ನಂಬಿಕೆಯಿಂದ. ವ್ಯವಹಾರಕ್ಕೆ ನಿಯಮಿತ ವಹಿವಾಟು, ಲಾಭದ ಉದ್ದೇಶ ಬೇಕು; ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಅಪಾಯವಿದೆ. ವ್ಯವಹಾರದ ಆದಾಯ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ. ಪ್ರಾಚೀನ ಭಾರತೀಯ ವ್ಯಾಪಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಹುಂಡಿಯಂತಹ ಸಾಧನಗಳು ಬಳಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದವು.
